newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty seen calm ahead of T-bill tender, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Zloty seen calm ahead of T-bill tender, depos flat.

text.p: The Polish zloty kept well below the central bank's intervention levels in early trade and dealers did not expect it to rise much today as foreign interest in the Polish T-bill tender was seen limited.
Dealers said foreign bids were likely to be spread between the T-bill auction and the 300 million two-year fixed bond tender on May 22.

"The zloty is not likely to test resistance levels at 2.5 percent from parity today because foreign interest in the tender does not seem huge, so an intervention against the zloty today is unlikely," said Karol Zaluski of ING bank in Warsaw.

At 0845 GMT the zloty was at 2.49/2.47 percent from the fixed parity rate for today, flat from opening. It was at 3.1465 against the dollar and 1.8570/75 against the mark, against 3.1460/70 and 1.8575/85 at opening respectively.
Money market rates were stable around 22.0 percent for overnight and tomorrow/next deposits even though the central bank said it would refrain from any open market operations.
Dealers said banks were not very keen to let out longer-term cash ahead of Wednesday's payments for T-bills bought at today's 1.3 billion zloty tender.

Yields were expected to ease at the auction amid large demand fuelled by Poland's good fundamentals, especially the drop in year-on-year price growth to 15.3 percent in April from 16.6 percent in March announced last Thursday.
The 52-week paper yield was seen down to 21.33 percent from 21.39 percent at the last tender.
